questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding serous cystic neoplasm of the pancreas except:

options.label: A
options.text: It is usually located in the tail

options.label: B
options.text: It is multicystic and contains clear, thin, straw-coloured fluid

options.label: C
options.text: It is a malignant tumour of the pancreas

options.label: D
options.text: Inactivation of the VHL gene is seen

questions.answerText: It is a malignant tumour of the pancreas
questions.solutionHtml:
It is a malignant tumour of the pancreas
  • Serous cystic neoplasm of the pancreas is a benign tumour and is typically located in the tail of the pancreas.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 686

questions.stem: All of the following are oncogenes mutated in pancreatic carcinoma except:
questions.solutionHtml:
SMAD 4
  • SMAD4 is not an oncogene but a tumour suppressor gene that is commonly inactivated in pancreatic cancer.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 686

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding pancreatic carcinoma except:

options.label: B
options.text: Cigarette smoking and diabetes are risk factors

options.label: C
options.text: The most favoured location is tail

options.label: D
options.text: Germline mutation can be seen in BRCA 2 and CDKN2A

questions.answerText: The most favoured location is tail
questions.solutionHtml:
The most favoured location is tail
  • Pancreatic carcinoma is most commonly seen in the head of the pancreas and not in the tail.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 686

questions.stemHtml: A 74-year-old patient presented with jaundice and a mass lesion in the head region of the pancreas in a CT scan. Biopsy from the lesion demonstrates as shown in the diagram. Based on the histological features what is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenocarcinoma
  • The given clinical history and an image showing glands lined by pleomorphic cuboidal-to-columnar epithelial cells suggest the diagnosis of Adenocarcinoma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 686
